note: First-round skeleton, section focus 1:50–2:17: VOSIM mouth and clean wire exchange the forward/backward hook every strip; an octave jump and then two toms mark the crossing before the guitars return.
v4, 2:25–2:33: the two reversed rows fold in to their centre; one clean F4 rings out and the full strip returns on low F.
v6: at 0:28 the right hand turns its palm strokes backwards before the tune turns. Three mutes, then five; both hands together at 0:35.6, before the v1 card.
v10: 0:54.8-1:05.8 the ribbon draws the top of what the two opposed guitars add up to (F, C, G flat, G flat, C, F), one unbroken sliding note that is its own mirror; it stops where the thumb starts.

v12: the last four strips of 'turn over' (3:11.8–3:22.8) move up to C, the strip's fourth open note and the one ground the song had not stood on; the forward hand's C chord is left ringing into it at 3:11.3 and 'one hand' begins on that C after the silence. The change starts in the last two seconds of w7, whose body is under the steel card and is as written.
v16: four strips of 'turn over' (2:55.4-3:06.3) read upside down: A flat, G flat, C become D, E, B flat; both hands heavy; a crash on each turn of the page

v17, the other hand reads it alone first: on the last strip of 'ink' (0:41.1-0:43.85) the band gives the downbeat and lifts off; the right guitar reads the strip from the far end by itself, with the hat's quarters, one strip before 'opposite'. The map: motion 0.0169 -> 0.0285.

v21: the other foot. 0:54.8-1:27.7 ('opposite' from its fifth strip): a second bass drum reads the right hand's open notes; from 1:16.7 each foot plays its hand's palm strokes too, sixteenths with three holes.

v24: the count is copied too, at its own length ('carbon', 1:27.7-1:49.6): the drummer's bars go page (sticks on the hat) and copy (the foot's hat); 16 against the hand's 19, so the two slip and come back
